design noun

a plan of how something will be made

also plans, blueprint, drawing

classical

Cic. Q. fr. 2.5.3: quam quantum ex fōrmā jūdicābāmus
Cic. Fam. 2.8.1: cum fōrmam reī pūblicae vīderim, quāle aedificium futūrum sit scīre possim

1fōrma: long o (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 233–234, s.v. fōrma, prints the o long; Ernout–Meillet “stress the length of o”, which he takes for a recent lengthening of short o before r and a consonant (Leumann 1977: 114).

fōrma1, fōrmae f.

noun, first declension

a design, an architect’s plan

The outline from which a building is judged before it stands (Lewis & Short: “an outline, plan, design (of an architect)”). To draw a design is dēscrībere (M-O s.v. design, citing Egger), as Archimedes drew his figures in the dust (fōrmīs, quās in pulvere dēscrīpserat, Liv. 25.31.9, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • dēscrīptiō, dēscrīptiōnis f. — a drawing, a plan; the layout of a building

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.138: aedificandī dēscrīptiō; Vitr. 3.3 (Lewis & Short: sketches)

    Cicero’s word for the plan of a house, which is to be fitted to its use (Off. 1.138).

  • ichnographia, ichnographiae f. — a ground plan

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Vitr. 1.2.2; M-O s.v. floor plan, ground plan, blueprint

    Vitruvius’s Greek term (ἰχνογραφία), for the technical drawing.

Examples

  • domus erit ēgregia; magis enim cernī jam poterat quam quantum ex fōrmā jūdicābāmus

    the house will be splendid: one can see more of it now than we could judge from the planCic. Q. fr. 2.5.3

See also plan, model, form, building site, design.

SourcesLewis & Short: forma · Lewis & Short: descriptio · Lewis & Short: ichnographia

Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), pp. 233–234.

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. design (vb.); floor plan, ground plan, blueprint.
